Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Rachel Park (Harbor Eng), Omar Ruiz (Harbor CTO), Jordan Lee (Harbor SRE)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): quick run through SDK auth and sandbox. talk about SSO and KMS. agreed to perf run.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference, and with me is Liam, our solutions engineer. Today's plan is a hands-on SDK walkthrough for Python and TypeScript, and we'll cover auth, sandbox env, and a couple Optimize tips.
[00:18] Rachel: Thanks, Maya. We're excited — Omar and Jordan are here to listen in on infra parts. Our main ask is we need a predictable latency under 150ms p95 for short prompts, and we also have strict keys rotation rules.
[00:35] Liam: Cool, sounds good. Quick question: are you planning hosted Redwood or private VPC later on?
[00:42] Omar: Likely private VPC for production, at least for the first year. For dev we're fine with hosted sandbox. Also we use Vault for secrets, so API key rotation is important.
[01:02] Maya: Great — we'll walk the hosted sandbox flow first and then call out the private deployment differences. I'll share the sandbox link and a short repo with examples.
[01:20] [screen share starts] Liam: On my screen is the Redwood Console. First, keys page: we create a scoped key for the sandbox with role limited to generation and embeddings. Note — the console UI sometimes labels "models" weirdly in the transcription, it showed as "modals" for a sec earlier, ignore that.
[01:45] Jordan: Quick question — can we attach key rotation policies from console or must it integrate with our Vault?
[01:52] Liam: For hosted keys, rotation is manual in console today; for automations you can use our KMS integrations. For Private VPC we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and you can plug Vault via the API. We'll include the KMS doc.
[02:13] Rachel: Could you show the Python quickstart? We prefer a small script to demo.
[02:20] Liam: Sure. Example: pip install redwood-client (note: package name is often misheard in transcript as red-wood or redwood inference client). Then minimal code: set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_API_URL and call client.generate("short prompt"). For TS it's similar; we show fetch with Authorization Bearer.
[02:45] [00:03:00] Maya: I'm going to paste the repo link in the chat: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sandbox-quickstarts (link provided as a note). It has python/ts examples, Dockerfile, and CI snippets.
[03:10] Rachel: On env vars — what variables do you recommend for local dev vs CI?
[03:17] Liam: Locally: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_API_URL (sandbox endpoint), and optionally REDWOOD_MODEL (default model id). For CI: prefer injecting secrets from Vault or Cloud KMS — don't hardcode. We'll send a sample GitHub Actions snippet.
[03:40] Omar: About network egress — for Private we'd need a VPC endpoint. Do you support private endpoints?
[03:48] Maya: Yes, Private supports VPC peering and endpoint proxies; we'll share the Private deployment runbook. For hosted sandbox no egress restrictions though.
[04:05] [00:05:00] Liam: Now, quick demo of Optimize settings: first rule is batching — for small requests we recommend a batch latency threshold of 20ms and a token cap per batch. Also prefix/KV cache is useful for chat use cases. In some docs you'll see it written as K V cache or KVcache — transcripts sometimes split it.
[04:32] Jordan: For our traffic pattern (many short 8-16 token calls) batching could harm p50. How do you tune?
[04:40] Liam: We expose per-route batching controls in the console; you can pin latency SLOs. For low-latency workloads we recommend smaller batch windows + warmed GPU pools (Dedicated). We'll include an Optimize recipe for qps <=200 and avg token length 12.
[05:05] Rachel: Anything about quantization or model family we should pick for cost?
[05:12] Liam: Short answer: smaller quantized variants reduce cost. We'll recommend model variants in the repo notes; we'll also run a quick perf benchmark during the pilot.
[05:28] Maya: Switching to auth nuance — we support API keys, SSO/SAML for the Console, and customer-managed KMS for Private. For tokens in app code, route requests through your backend to avoid leaking keys in browser.
[05:50] [00:10:00] Omar: On compliance: we need SOC2 plus audit logs retention for 1 year. How do you expose audit logs?
[05:58] Liam: Audit logs are available for Private and Dedicated, and for Hosted we can provide longer retention as an add-on. Logs include per-request metadata and model version. We'll send the SOC2 summary and log retention options.
[06:20] Rachel: Can we see an example of the TypeScript snippet for server-side calls?
[06:26] Liam: Yes — here's a sample using node-fetch: const res = await fetch(process.env.REDWOOD_API_URL + '/v1/generate', { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`}, method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({model: 'rwd-opt-1', input: 'hello'})}); Then res.json(). We also show streaming with EventSource in the repo.
[06:52] [00:15:00] Maya: A couple of gotchas we've seen: don't set overly long max tokens for short prompts (wastes cost), and when moving to Dedicated set instance warm-up so KV cache warms.
[07:10] Jordan: For performance testing, what tooling do you recommend?
[07:16] Liam: We usually give a JMeter/Postman collection and a small runner that replays your sample distribution. We'll include a benchmark harness in the sandbox repo.
[07:32] Rachel: On permissions — can we create role-based keys so product teams only have access to embeddings and not generation?
[07:39] Liam: Yes, we support scoped keys with fine-grained scopes in the console. For private setups you can map to your IAM roles.
[08:00] [00:20:00] (noise/crosstalk) Speaker 2: um yeah, saw the console, can you show the rollback or canary deploy process?
[08:08] Maya: Sure. Rollouts are managed via model version pinning and route-level fallbacks. You can create a canary route that sends e.g. 5% to new model, and Redwood will auto-fallback on errors. We'll send the rollout playbook PDF.
[08:35] Omar: One more security detail — encryption at rest for logs and user data: do you support customer keys?
[08:42] Liam: For Private and Dedicated yes, you can use your KMS. For Hosted we store with provider-managed keys but can offer BYOK contracts for enterprise.
[08:58] Rachel: Any examples for secret rotation in CI?
[09:03] Maya: We'll share a GitHub Actions sample that pulls secrets from Vault and rotates them via the API — that will be in the repo.
[09:20] [00:30:00] Liam: Demoing a quick local dev flow: start with docker-compose that runs a tiny proxy which injects REDWOOD_API_KEY from Vault. The repo has an example compose. For testing we use the sandbox endpoint which has limited quotas but mirrors production routing.
[09:45] Rachel: How do we ingest embeddings? Our vector store is Pinecone — any compatibility notes?
[09:52] Liam: We generate embeddings and then push to Pinecone. Nothing special; we provide an example connector in TS that shows batching embeddings by 100 and upserting. For dense vectors we recommend 32-bit floats by default but you can quantize.
[10:15] Maya: Quick callout: some transcripts and docs mistakenly call the product Redwood Inference's "Optimize" part as "Opti-mize" (two words) — it's one word.
[10:28] Jordan: (laughs) noted.
[10:35] [00:40:00] Omar: For the pilot timeline, we aim to run a 2-week sandbox pilot, then a perf run, then decide Dedicated/private by mid-August. Does that align?
[10:44] Maya: Yes. We'll target sandbox start Monday (2025-07-28), perf run week of 2025-08-04, and a decision checkpoint 2025-08-15.
[11:00] Rachel: Any immediate blockers on our side? We need the sample traffic generator and the Small sample dataset for testing.
[11:07] Liam: We'll drop both in the repo and in the sandbox. Also will add a sample config for Vault integration.
[11:22] Maya: Recap: Liam will provision sandbox + repo updates; Maya will send security docs and pricing sketch; Harbor team will schedule infra follow-up.
[11:35] [00:50:00] (wrap-up) Omar: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[11:40] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up by EOD Monday with the links.
[11:45] Rachel: Great, bye.
